test_title: PYST 65: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When an object is moved slowly and gradually closer to a convex mirror from infinity towards the pole (P), what can we say about the image?

options.text: Moves from the pole (P) towards the principal focus (F)
Moves from the principal focus (F) towards the pole (P)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Moves from the principal focus (F) towards the pole (P)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **convex mirror** is a spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards. It is also known as a **diverging mirror** because it diverges light rays after reflection.
 
• When an object is placed at **infinity**, the rays of light are parallel to the principal axis. These rays appear to diverge from the **principal focus (F)** after reflection. Therefore, the image is formed at **focus (F)** behind the mirror and is **virtual**, **erect**, and **highly diminished**.
 
• As the object is moved from **infinity** towards the **pole (P)** of the mirror, the **virtual image** shifts its position from the **principal focus (F)** toward the **pole (P)**.
